newsitem.title: USA: Search continues for source of La. natgas leak.
newsitem.headline: Search continues for source of La. natgas leak.

text.p: The U.S. Coast Guard on Friday said crews were still trying to determine the source of a natural gas leak in the onshore waters of Louisiana's Vermilion Bay.
Three of five pipelines threading through the area where bubbles have been spotted on the surface have been shut in and two others were ordered shut in and tested, a Coast Guard spokesman said.
"We're still trying to find who it is," Coast Guard Petty Officer Chip Thompson said. "Most of them are still shut in from yesterday. We're going to find out today who it is."

Acadian Gas Pipeline, Louisiana Resources Co, Sea Robin Pipeline and Texas Gas Transmission Corp each operate major pipelines running through the bay waters about 40 miles south of Lafayette, La., a state pipeline official said.
The leak was believed to be small and there was no oil sheen, and the Coast Guard expects to have the leaking pipeline identified by midday, Thompson said.
Traders said news of the leak was a factor in pushing the market higher last night, but one Houston trader said the large pipelines in the area confirmed overnight their lines were not leaking.
Checks early Friday with ipeline operators linked to the system so far showed no significant interruptions to gas flows.
